Annotation-gated INI/XML/CLI processing does not authorize assignments to arbitrary unannotated selector fields. assessment.conclusion: The wrapper names the normal dedicated Editor target and supplies no test-target switch. Complete target creation and PreBuildSetup distinguish selected plugin modules, extra modules and recursive dependencies from AddAllValidModulesToTarget. The latter remains conditional on bBuildAllModules. Its alternative platform, module-validity, plugin-choice, disable, program and precompile filters do not imply catalog-wide building or runtime activation.

assessment.conclusion: Receipt preparation, metadata scheduling and serialization preserve project/target/platform/configuration identity, launch paths, explicit target plugin overrides, build-plugin names and additional properties. BuildPlugins serves an optional-dependency allowlist in the relevant runtime consumer; it is not a runtime-enable root list. The wrapper requires exactly one staged dedicated target receipt, its staged project and installed Editor/Editor-Cmd launch identities, and the exact proof override/default policy. Runtime receipt lookup prefers the project and matching executable before engine fallback.
assessment.qualification: The wrapper validates BuildPlugins element shape and records its allowlist meaning; it does not validate that array as the complete runtime-enable set.

assessment.conclusion: Launch environment insertion precedes plugin selection; the wrapper clears UE-CmdLineArgs and UE_ADDITIONAL_PLUGIN_PATHS. Runtime command-line plugin configuration precedes receipts, project references and defaults. Configured-name suppression of later roots does not itself prohibit dependency expansion. No selected conservative parent has an enabled dependency on any of the six disabled names. Receipt/default policy and project policy are distinct: project processing can overwrite the receipt-derived default flag; the supplied project's absent disabling flag and the reviewed receipt policy both permit defaults.

The complete startup dispatcher loads project modules before plugin modules at PreDefault, Default and PostDefault, returns false on failure, and is called by PreInitPostStartupScreen with failure propagated as exit status 1. Ordinary plugin dispatch requires enabled state and excludes ExplicitlyLoaded plugins. Module phase, compiled/runtime host conditions and already-loaded checks apply. The proof descriptor places parser before probe at Default; both module entry implementations use FDefaultModuleImpl and add no explicit plugin-mount startup route.

Public MountExplicitlyLoadedPlugin and private MountPluginFromExternalSource declarations both supply ELoadingPhase::Max as the omitted maximum argument. Explicit mounting iterates phases below that maximum and skips None. It ignores TryLoadModulesForPlugin failures, marks the plugin mounted and can return success without successful module startup. Filename/descriptor variants additionally resolve or promote a version and reject an already-mounted conflicting version. The complete supplied PluginUtils, Fab, Pak virtualization, GDK DLC, Game Features and low-level-test callers were assessed with their creation, download, initialization, platform, state-machine, policy, configuration and test gates. Their presence does not establish execution in this proof.
assessment.qualification: The explicit-mount return limitation is relevant engine behavior, not evidence that the ordinary proof Default route executed unsuccessfully.

assessment.conclusion: The target-to-module interface joins the pinned acquisition/artifact/header identities, held read locks, Win64 Development x64 guards, selected toolchain/SDK, static yaml-cpp linkage, C++20 and dynamic release CRT requirements with the parser/probe module settings. Its source also preserves the 33-member stage contract, owned outputs and fixture inputs, nine settings roles, six supervisor controls, process/job/exit/timeout evidence and ordered single-phase predecessors.
